Great question! Argus doesn't help you *discover* new stocks to invest in — it's more of a "test your idea" tool. You bring the asset (like a specific stock, crypto, or currency pair), and Argus runs a backtest experiment on it using a strategy you choose.

So if you already have a stock in mind and want to see how a simple moving average crossover or dollar-cost averaging would have performed, Argus can do that. But finding new stocks to watch? That's outside what Argus supports — no stock screeners or recommendations here.

If you have a particular stock or asset you're curious about, I can help you set up an experiment to test a strategy on it!
Argus does not support options strategies such as straddles. It can run long-only equity backtests like buy and hold or RSI mean reversion on TSLA over the same dates if that works instead.
